limitations: A single archive with 200001 original messages resolves only the first 200000 and explicitly returns incomplete=true. A search for the omitted tail returns no hit and no cursor; direct tail selection returns source-not-in-archive even though the original event remains stored. This is bounded partial retrieval, not full archival reachability.

Across separate nested archives, search ownership tracking at 200000 entries retains a late source but can return it twice; the duplicate allowance was observed. After traversing 34 separate archives, an earlier active cursor still recovered all original Unicode/CRLF bytes after the source cache evicted its entry.

These detached real-host Session checks use a 1024 MiB heap ceiling and no provider calls. R20 retains five heap-exhaustion failures at 100000 events / 8 sessions under 512 MiB; no broad resource-safety pass is claimed.
